edges.description: The germline AIP loss-of-function allele acts as the first ("inherited") hit; a somatic second hit at the wild-type AIP locus on 11q13 (loss of heterozygosity / large-scale chromosomal deletion) completes biallelic inactivation per the Knudson two-hit tumor-suppressor model.
Somatic loss of the remaining AIP allele eliminates residual AIP function in the tumor-initiating somatotroph clone.
Loss of AIP perturbs its co-chaperone binding to the aryl hydrocarbon receptor.
AIP deficiency disrupts GNAI2 and GNAI3 function, weakening inhibitory G-protein restraint of adenylate cyclase and cAMP synthesis.
AIP deficiency disrupts an AIP-PDE module that normally binds and modulates PDE4A-family cAMP phosphodiesterase control.
AIP-mutant somatotroph cells express less SSTR2, weakening the receptor target used by first-generation somatostatin analogs.
edges.target: Reduced SSTR2 expression in AIP-mutant somatotrophs

edges.description: AIP-mutant somatotroph cells express less PLAGL1/ZAC1, reducing a tumor-suppressor program that normally restrains proliferation.
AIP-mutant somatotroph cells show increased IL-6 and phosphorylated STAT3, linking the AIP-deficient state to a cytokine-signaling program.
Disruption of AIP-dependent AHR complex handling dysregulates AHR target-gene transcriptional responses.
AIP-dependent disruption of AHR signaling affects kynurenine-dependent growth hormone secretion in pituitary GH3 cells.
Failure of GNAI2/GNAI3-mediated adenylate cyclase restraint elevates cAMP signaling in AIP-deficient somatotrophs.
Loss of the AIP-dependent PDE4A module reduces the PDE4A4/PDE4A8 compensation that normally degrades cAMP in somatotroph tumors.
Reduced PDE4A4/PDE4A8 expression limits cAMP degradation, feeding into elevated cAMP/PKA signaling.
Elevated cAMP/PKA signaling contributes to development of large, GH-secreting pituitary adenomas in AIP mutation carriers.
The AIP-deficient cAMP program favors a GH-secreting somatotroph tumor phenotype.
Defective cAMP restraint in AIP mutation carriers contributes to GH-secreting pituitary adenoma development within the AIP-related predisposition spectrum.
AIP-related adenomas include mixed GH/PRL-secreting and PRL-secreting tumors; the specific mechanistic bridge from the somatotroph cAMP branch to prolactin excess remains unresolved.
Loss of the ZAC1 tumor-suppressor program contributes to increased proliferation and invasion in AIP-mutant somatotroph cells.
IL-6/phospho-STAT3 activation contributes to the proliferative and invasive AIP-mutant somatotroph phenotype.
IL-6/phospho-STAT3 activation is associated with GH secretion in AIP-mutant somatotroph cells.
Increased somatotroph proliferation and invasion contribute to large, aggressive pituitary adenomas.
Large AIP-associated pituitary macroadenomas can cause headache through sellar mass effect.
Suprasellar extension of large AIP-associated pituitary tumors can cause visual field loss by optic apparatus compression.
Large pituitary macroadenomas can cause headache through local sellar mass effect.
Suprasellar macroadenoma extension can compress the optic apparatus and cause visual field loss.

nodes.description: AIP normally participates as a co-chaperone/scaffold in a phosphodiesterase module that includes PDE4A isoforms.
